ko.title: [소매 101 #13] 선반이 비워질 때까지 아무도 공급망을 모른다

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > 소매업자의 진정한 상품은 단순히 선반에 있는 것이 아니라 재고에 빠져서 망하지 않으면서 날마다 그것을 유지할 수 있는 능력이다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: 어느 슈퍼마켓에 들어가든 선반은 쉬워 보인다.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: 그것은 착각이다.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: 가득 찬 모든 선반 뒤에는 *얼마나* 많이 옮길지, *언제*, 그리고 *어디로* 옮길지에 대한 일련의 결정이 있다 — 그리고 그런 결정을 틀리는 소매업자는 상품이 떨어지거나 아무도 아직 구매하지 않는 물건에 수백만 달러를 묶어둔다.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: 세 가지 요소가 이 체계를 이룬다.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: 배포 센터(DC).** 대부분의 연쇄 소매업자는 공장에서 각 점포로 배송하지 않는다.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: 그렇다면 핫소스 공급자가 400개의 별도 주소로 소량 배송을 해야 한다.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: 대신 공급자는 지역 DC에 가득 찬 트럭을 보낸다 — 큰 건물로, 종종 50만~100만 제곱피트이며, 보통 주간 고속도로 근처에 위치해서 트럭이 하루 안에 점포에 도달할 수 있도록 한다.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: DC는 그 트럭 적재분을 분해하고 혼합 적재분으로 재구성한다: 한 점포에 한 트럭, 칩 *그리고* 휴지 *그리고* 샴푸를 실은.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: 트럭 수는 적어지고, 트럭은 더 가득 찬다, 케이스당 비용이 더 낮다.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: 더 빠른 변형은 **크로스 도킹**이다: 상품이 인바운드 도크에 도착하고 정렬되어 몇 시간 내에 아웃바운드 트럭으로 떠난다, 저장소에 들어가지 않는다.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: 빠른 회전 상품과 신선한 농산물에 좋다; 실수를 숨길 버퍼가 없기 때문에 매우 긴밀한 조율이 필요하다.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: 재고 보충.** 이것은 언제 재주문할지에 대한 질문이다.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: 고전적 논리:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: 점포가 하루에 20개를 판매하고 더 얻는 데 3일이 걸리면, 60개에서 재주문해야 한다 — 더하기 주 중 수요가 급증하거나 트럭이 늦을 때를 위한 완충.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: 그 완충은 **안전 재고**이고, 명시적 거래다: 더 많은 안전 재고는 더 적은 품절과 선반에 앉아있는 더 많은 현금을 의미한다.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: 오늘날 대부분은 판매점 스캔 데이터에서 자동으로 작동하므로, 계산대 스캐너는 단순한 현금 등록기가 아니라 공급망 도구다.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: 공급망 관리(SCM).** SCM은 공급자, DC, 운송, 점포 전반에 걸친 조율 계층이다 — 각각 자체적으로 최적화하는 부서 대신 하나의 시스템으로 취급한다.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: 이것이 존재하여 방지하려는 고전적 실패는 **불채찍 효과**다: 고객 수요의 작은 변동이 상류로 이동할 때 증폭된다.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: 점포가 5% 증가를 보고, 안전하게 10% 더 주문하고, DC가 20% 더 주문하고, 공급자가 40% 더 많은 용량을 구축한다 — 그리고 나서 그 증가가 아무것도 아니라는 것이 드러난다.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: 상류 모든 사람들이 재고를 들고 남겨진다.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: 해결책은 정보다: 각 링크가 받은 주문에서 추측하도록 하는 대신 실제 판매 데이터를 공유한다.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: 그것이 공급자가 소매업자의 실제 판매를 보고 무엇을 배송할지 결정하는 **공급자 관리 재고(VMI)**같은 계약이 존재하는 이유다.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: 월마트와 프록터 앤 갬블은 1980년대 후반에 이것의 초기 유명한 버전을 구축했고, 그 모델은 업계 전반에 퍼졌다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: 슈퍼볼 전 토요일이다.

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: 당신은 피닉스 밖의 슈퍼마켓에 있고, 토르티야 칩과 살사를 원한다.

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: 작동해야 할 것들은 다음과 같다.

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: 3주 전, 카테고리 계획자가 지난해 숫자를 살펴보고 이 점포가 2일 기간에 평소 칩 거래량의 대략 6배를 판매할 것이라고 예측했다.

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: 그 예측은 공급자에게 더 큰 구매 주문을 유발했다.

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: 칩은 트럭 적재분으로 주간 고속도로 근처, 약 30마일 떨어진 체인의 DC로 배송되었다.

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: 밤새 DC 근로자들이 지역의 각 점포에 대한 케이스를 픽업하고 혼합 트레일러를 로드했다.

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: 그것은 오전 4시에 당신의 점포에 도착했고, 승무원들이 당신이 깨기 전에 엔드캡 디스플레이에 재고를 적재했다.

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: 이제 뒤집어보자.

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: 예측이 40% 빗나갔다고 가정하자.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: 두 가지 결과, 둘 다 비싸다:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **너무 적다.** 빈 선반을 찾고, 경쟁사로 차를 몰고 가고, 체인은 $6 가방 *그리고* 당신이 그 주변에 채웠을 $80 장바구니를 잃는다. 널리 인용되는 소매 연구에 따르면 평균 품절률은 전 세계적으로 8% 범위 어딘가에 있다 — 작게 들리지만 판매에 직접 영향을 미친다.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **너무 많다.** 월요일이 되면, 점포는 주 단위로 측정되는 유통기한을 가진 스낵의 추가 200개 가방을 가지고 있고, 그들은 50% 할인으로 판매될 것이다 — 원가 이하로 판매되고, 1개월 동안 그들에 묶여있던 현금도 포함한다.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: 둘 다 광고나 점포 디자인에 나타나지 않는다.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: 둘 다 손익계산서에 나타난다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. 배포 센터는 공급자 배송을 점포를 위한 가득 차고 혼합된 트럭 적재분으로 통합하기 위해 존재한다 — 케이스당 비용 절감; 크로스 도킹은 아무것도 저장하지 않고 그렇게 한다.

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. 재고 보충은 리드 타임과 안전 재고에 관한 수학 문제다: 너무 적으면 판매 손실, 너무 많으면 묵인된 현금과 인하다.

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. SCM은 전체 체인을 조율하고 각 링크가 추측하도록 하는 대신 실제 수요 데이터를 공유함으로써 불채찍 효과에 대항한다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가진단 퀴즈

segments.tr: **Q1.** 크로스 도킹에서, 수입된 상품은 점포로 배송되기 전에 DC 저장소에서 몇 주 동안 보관된다.

segments.tr: (O / X)

segments.tr: **Q2.** 점포는 평균적으로 하루에 30개를 판매하고, 공급자 리드 타임은 4일이고, 40개 안전 재고를 유지한다.

segments.src: What is its reorder point?
segments.tr: 그것의 재주문 포인트는 무엇인가?

segments.src: - (a) 70 units
- (b) 120 units
- (c) 160 units

**Q3.** Which of the following best describes the bullwhip effect?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 다음 중 불채찍 효과를 가장 잘 설명하는 것은?

segments.src: - (a) Retail prices rise faster than wholesale prices during inflation
segments.tr: - (a) 소매 가격이 인플레이션 중에 도매 가격보다 빠르게 오른다

segments.src: - (b) Demand variability grows larger at each step further upstream in the supply chain
segments.tr: - (b) 수요 변동이 공급망에서 상류로 갈수록 각 단계에서 더 커진다

segments.src: - (c) Stores near a DC get deliveries faster than distant stores
segments.tr: - (c) DC 근처 점포가 먼 점포보다 빠르게 배송을 받는다

segments.src: - (d) Shoppers buy more when a product is displayed at eye level
segments.tr: - (d) 쇼핑객들은 상품이 눈높이에 표시될 때 더 많이 구매한다

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **배포 센터(DC):** 공급자로부터 대량 배송을 받아서 혼합된 점포용 적재분으로 재배포하는 시설.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **크로스 도킹:** 인바운드 도크에서 아웃바운드 도크로 상품을 최소한의 저장으로 옮기는 것.

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **리드 타임:** 주문을 배치하는 것부터 상품이 판매 가능해질 때까지의 경과 시간.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **안전 재고:** 수요 급증과 배송 지연에 대한 버퍼로 유지되는 추가 재고.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **불채찍 효과:** 주문이 점포에서 공급자로 이동할 때 수요 변동의 증폭.

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **공급자 관리 재고(VMI):** 공급자가 소매업자의 판매 데이터를 사용하여 무엇과 언제 배송할지 결정하는 계약.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *답변: **Q1 — X.** 크로스 도킹은 저장소의 부재로 정의되고; 상품은 보통 몇 시간 내에 떠난다.

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b).** 불채찍 효과는 각 링크가 실제 최종 고객 수요보다는 그 아래의 링크에서 주문함으로써 야기되는 수요 변동의 상류 증폭이다.

segments.src: Sharing point-of-sale data is the standard remedy.*
segments.tr: 판매점 데이터 공유가 표준 치료법이다.*

zh.title: [零售101 #13] 货架空了才知道供应链的重要性

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > 零售商的真正产品不仅仅是货架上的商品——而是日复一日地保持货架满满的能力，而不被过量库存所淹没。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: 走进任何超市，货架看起来毫不费力。

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: 这就是假象。

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: 每一个满满的货架后面都隐藏着一系列的决策——*移动多少*、*何时*以及*移向何处*——如果零售商做出了错误的决定，要么缺货，要么将数百万美元的资金压在还没人买的商品上。

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: 三个部分组成了这个体系。

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: 配送中心（DC）。** 大多数连锁零售商不会直接从工厂发货到每家门店。

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: 那意味着一个辣酱供应商要向400个不同的地址发送小件货物。

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: 相反，供应商会向一个地区配送中心发送满载的卡车——一栋很大的建筑，通常面积在50万到100多万平方英尺，通常位于州际公路附近，这样卡车一天内就能到达各家门店。

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: 配送中心将这些满载的货物拆分，重新组合成混合负载：一辆卡车送到一家门店，运送薯片*和*纸巾*和*洗发水。

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: 卡车数量更少，装载更满，单位成本更低。

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: 一个更快的变体是**交叉转运**：产品到达入境码头，进行分类，然后在数小时内离开出境卡车，从不进入仓库。

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: 非常适合快速流转的商品和新鲜农产品；它需要极其紧密的协调，因为没有缓冲来隐藏错误。

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: 补货。** 这是何时补货的问题。

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: 经典的逻辑是：

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: 如果一家门店每天销售20件，补货需要3天，那么它应该在60件时补货——加上一个缓冲以应对周需求激增或卡车延迟。

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: 这个缓冲就是**安全库存**，这是一个明确的权衡：更多的安全库存意味着更少的缺货和更多的现金压在货架上。

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: 如今，大多数这类工作都通过销售点扫描数据自动运行，这就是为什么收银扫描仪是供应链工具，而不仅仅是收银机。

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: 供应链管理（SCM）。** SCM是跨供应商、配送中心、运输和门店的协调层——将它们视为一个系统，而不是各自优化的部门。

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: 它存在的目的是防止**牛鞭效应**这一经典失败：客户需求的小幅波动在向上游传导时会被放大。

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: 一家门店看到需求增长5%，为了安全起见多订购10%，配送中心多订购20%，供应商增加40%的产能——然后这个增长转向为零。

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: 上游所有人都被迫持有库存。

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: 解决办法是信息共享：共享真实销售数据，而不是让供应链的每个环节根据接收到的订单进行猜测。

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: 这就是**供应商管理库存（VMI）**等安排存在的原因，其中供应商看到零售商的实际销售额并决定运送什么。

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: 沃尔玛和宝洁公司在20世纪80年代末建立了这一著名的早期版本，该模式后来在整个行业传播开来。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: 这是美国超级杯前的星期六。

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: 你在菲尼克斯郊外的一家超市，想要玉米饼干和莎莎酱。

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: 以下是需要协调运作的内容。

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: 三周前，一位商品规划师查看了去年的数据，预测这家门店在两天内的薯片销售量大约是正常销售量的六倍。

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: 这个预测促使向供应商下达了更大的采购订单。

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: 薯片通过卡车运送到连锁店靠近州际公路的配送中心，距离约30英里。

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: 一夜之间，配送中心的工人为该地区的每家门店挑选商品并装上混合拖车。

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: 它在凌晨4点到达你的门店，一支工作人员在你醒来前摆放了一个端点展示架。

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: 现在反过来看。

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: 假设预测偏差40%。

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: 两种结果，都很昂贵：

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **库存过少。** 你发现货架是空的，驾车去竞争对手那里，连锁店失去了一个$6的商品*加上*你本来会购买的$80的购物篮。 广泛引用的零售研究表明，全球平均缺货率在8%左右——听起来很小，但它直接影响销售。

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **库存过多。** 到了星期一，门店有200个额外的零食袋，保质期以周计，它们以50%的折扣销售——亏本销售，加上被压在其中一个月的现金。

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: 这两种情况都不会出现在广告或门店设计中。

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: 但都会出现在利润表中。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. 配送中心的存在是为了将供应商的货物整合成满载的、混合的卡车运往门店——降低单位成本；交叉转运可以不存储任何东西的情况下完成这一点。

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. 补货是一个关于提前期和安全库存的数学问题：过少意味着失去销售，过多意味着现金被压死和价格下降。

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. SCM协调整个供应链，通过共享真实需求数据而不是让每个环节进行猜测来对抗牛鞭效应。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **Q1.** In cross-docking, incoming goods are held in DC storage for several weeks before being shipped to stores.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 在交叉转运中，入库商品在配送中心存储数周后才被运往门店。

segments.src: (O / X)
segments.tr: （O / X）

segments.src: **Q2.** A store sells an average of 30 units a day, its supplier lead time is 4 days, and it keeps 40 units of safety stock.
segments.tr: **Q2.** 一家门店平均每天销售30件，其供应商提前期为4天，保持40件安全库存。

segments.src: What is its reorder point?
segments.tr: 其补货点是多少？

segments.src: - (a) 70 units
- (b) 120 units
- (c) 160 units
- (d) 200 units
**Q3.** Which of the following best describes the bullwhip effect?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 以下哪一项最好地描述了牛鞭效应？

segments.src: - (a) Retail prices rise faster than wholesale prices during inflation
segments.tr: - (a) 通货膨胀期间零售价格比批发价格上升更快

segments.src: - (b) Demand variability grows larger at each step further upstream in the supply chain
segments.tr: - (b) 需求波动性在供应链中每向上游走一步就会增大

segments.src: - (c) Stores near a DC get deliveries faster than distant stores
segments.tr: - (c) 靠近配送中心的门店比远离的门店获得交付的速度更快

segments.src: - (d) Shoppers buy more when a product is displayed at eye level
segments.tr: - (d) 当产品在眼睛水平线上展示时，购物者购买更多

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **配送中心（DC）：** 从供应商接收大宗货物并将其重新分配为混合的、准备好的门店货物的设施。

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **交叉转运：** 在很少或没有中间存储的情况下，将货物从入站码头移动到出站码头。

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **提前期：** 从下单到商品可供销售的经过时间。

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **安全库存：** 作为需求激增和交付延迟缓冲而持有的额外库存。

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **牛鞭效应：** 当订单从门店向供应商传导时需求波动的放大。

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **供应商管理库存（VMI）：** 供应商使用零售商的销售数据来决定运送什么和何时运送的安排。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 — X。** 交叉转运的特点是没有存储；产品通常在数小时内离开。

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b)。** 牛鞭效应是需求波动性的上游放大，由供应链的每个环节根据其下游环节的订单而不是真实最终客户需求进行订购而造成。

segments.src: Sharing point-of-sale data is the standard remedy.*
segments.tr: 共享销售点数据是标准的解决方案。*

hi.title: [खुदरा 101 #13] जब तक अलमारी खाली न हो, कोई भी आपूर्ति श्रृंखला पर ध्यान नहीं देता

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > एक खुदरा विक्रेता का असली उत्पाद केवल अलमारी पर जो है वह नहीं है — यह इसे हर दिन रखने की क्षमता है, इन्वेंटरी में डूबे बिना।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: किसी भी सुपरमार्केट में चलें और अलमारियां आसान दिखती हैं।

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: यह भ्रम है।

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: हर भरी हुई अलमारी के पीछे निर्णयों की एक श्रृंखला है कि *कितना* स्थानांतरित करना है, *कब*, और *कहाँ* — और एक खुदरा विक्रेता जो उन निर्णयों को गलत तरीके से लेता है या तो उत्पाद से बाहर चला जाता है या लाखों डॉलर को उस सामान में बांध देता है जिसे अभी कोई नहीं खरीद रहा है।

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: तीन भाग मशीनरी बनाते हैं।

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: वितरण केंद्र (DC)।** अधिकांश श्रृंखला खुदरा विक्रेता कारखाने से प्रत्येक स्टोर को शिप नहीं करते हैं।

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: इसका मतलब यह होगा कि एक गर्म सॉस आपूर्तिकर्ता 400 अलग पते पर छोटी डिलीवरी भेजता है।

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: इसके बजाय, आपूर्तिकर्ता एक क्षेत्रीय DC को पूर्ण ट्रकलोड भेजते हैं — एक बड़ी इमारत, अक्सर 500,000 से 1 मिलियन-प्लस वर्ग फीट, आमतौर पर राजमार्गों के पास स्थित ताकि ट्रक एक दिन में अपने स्टोर तक पहुंच सके।

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: DC उन ट्रकलोड को अलग करता है और उन्हें मिश्रित लोड में फिर से बनाता है: एक ट्रक से एक स्टोर, चिप्स *और* कागज के तौलिए *और* शैम्पू ले जाता है।

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: कम ट्रक, अधिक भरे हुए ट्रक, प्रति केस कम लागत।

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: एक तेजी संस्करण **क्रॉस-डॉकिंग** है: उत्पाद इनबाउंड डॉक पर आता है, छांटा जाता है, और कुछ घंटों के भीतर आउटबाउंड ट्रक पर निकल जाता है, कभी भी भंडारण में प्रवेश नहीं करता है।

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: तेजी से चलने वाली वस्तुओं और ताजे उपज के लिए बहुत अच्छा; इसके लिए बहुत कसा हुआ समन्वय की आवश्यकता है, क्योंकि गलतियों को छिपाने के लिए कोई बफर नहीं है।

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: पुनः पूर्ति।** यह सवाल है कि कब फिर से ऑर्डर करना है।

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: क्लासिक तर्क:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: यदि एक स्टोर एक दिन में 20 इकाइयां बेचता है और अधिक प्राप्त करने में 3 दिन लगते हैं, तो इसे 60 इकाइयों पर फिर से ऑर्डर करना चाहिए — साथ ही सप्ताह की मांग में वृद्धि या ट्रक देर से आने के लिए एक कुशन।

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: वह कुशन **सुरक्षा स्टॉक** है, और यह एक स्पष्ट व्यापार है: अधिक सुरक्षा स्टॉक का मतलब कम स्टॉकआउट और अधिक नकदी अलमारी पर बैठी है।

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: आजकल इनमें से अधिकांश बिक्री बिंदु स्कैन डेटा से स्वचालित रूप से चलता है, जिस कारण चेकआउट स्कैनर एक आपूर्ति श्रृंखला उपकरण है, न कि केवल एक नकद रजिस्टर।

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: आपूर्ति श्रृंखला प्रबंधन (SCM)।** SCM आपूर्तिकर्ताओं, DCs, परिवहन और स्टोर में समन्वय परत है — उन्हें एक प्रणाली के रूप में माना जाता है न कि विभागों के रूप में जो प्रत्येक स्वयं को अनुकूलित करते हैं।

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: क्लासिक विफलता जिसे रोकने के लिए यह मौजूद है **bullwhip प्रभाव** है: ग्राहक मांग में छोटी गड़बड़ी बढ़ जाती है जब वे अपस्ट्रीम जाते हैं।

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: एक स्टोर 5% की वृद्धि देखता है, सुरक्षित होने के लिए 10% अधिक ऑर्डर करता है, DC 20% अधिक ऑर्डर करता है, आपूर्तिकर्ता 40% अधिक क्षमता बनाता है — और फिर वृद्धि कुछ नहीं निकलती है।

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: अपस्ट्रीम का हर कोई इन्वेंटरी पकड़े हुए रह जाता है।

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: समाधान जानकारी है: वास्तविक बिक्री डेटा साझा करें बजाय प्रत्येक लिंक को यह अनुमान लगाने देने के कि इसे मिलने वाले आदेशों से।

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि **विक्रेता-प्रबंधित इन्वेंटरी (VMI)** जैसी व्यवस्थाएं मौजूद हैं, जहां आपूर्तिकर्ता खुदरा विक्रेता की वास्तविक बिक्री देखता है और तय करता है कि क्या शिप करना है।

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: सुपर बाउल से पहले शनिवार है।

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: आप फीनिक्स के बाहर एक सुपरमार्केट में हैं, और आप टॉर्टिला चिप्स और साल्सा चाहते हैं।

segments.tr: यहाँ वह है जो काम करना था।

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: तीन सप्ताह पहले, एक श्रेणी योजनाकार ने पिछले साल की संख्याओं को देखा और पूर्वानुमान लगाया कि यह स्टोर दो दिन की खिड़की में अपनी सामान्य चिप मात्रा से लगभग छह गुना बेचेगा।

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: दो परिणाम, दोनों महंगे:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **बहुत कम।** आप एक खाली अलमारी पाते हैं, एक प्रतिद्वंद्वी के पास जाते हैं, और श्रृंखला $6 बैग *प्लस* $80 बास्केट खो देता है जिसे आप इसके चारों ओर भरते। व्यापक रूप से उद्धृत खुदरा अनुसंधान ने औसत स्टॉक-आउट दरों को दुनिया भर में 8% की सीमा में डाला है — छोटा लगता है, लेकिन यह सीधे बिक्री पर गिरता है।

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **बहुत ज्यादा।** सोमवार को, स्टोर के पास 200 अतिरिक्त बैग हैं एक स्नैक का जिसकी शेल्फ लाइफ हफ्तों में मापी जाती है, और वे 50% ऑफ पर चले जाएंगे — लागत से नीचे बेचे गए, साथ ही नकदी जो एक महीने के लिए उनमें बंद थी।

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.

segments.tr: दोनों P&L में दिखाई देते हैं।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-लाइन पुनरावृत्ति

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. वितरण केंद्र आपूर्तिकर्ता शिपमेंट को पूर्ण, मिश्रित ट्रकलोड में समेकित करने के लिए स्टोर के लिए मौजूद हैं — प्रति केस लागत काट रहे हैं; क्रॉस-डॉकिंग इसे कुछ भी संग्रहीत किए बिना करता है।

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. पुनः पूर्ति एक गणितीय समस्या है लीड समय और सुरक्षा स्टॉक के बारे में: बहुत कम का मतलब है खोई हुई बिक्री, बहुत अधिक का मतलब है मृत नकदी और अंकन।

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. SCM पूरी श्रृंखला को समन्वयित करता है और वास्तविक मांग डेटा साझा करके बुलव्हिप प्रभाव से लड़ता है बजाय प्रत्येक लिंक को अनुमान लगाने दें।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **वितरण केंद्र (DC):** एक सुविधा जो आपूर्तिकर्ताओं से थोक शिपमेंट प्राप्त करती है और उन्हें मिश्रित, स्टोर-तैयार लोड के रूप में पुनः वितरित करती है।

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **क्रॉस-डॉकिंग:** सामान को इनबाउंड डॉक से आउटबाउंड डॉक में कम या कोई भंडारण के साथ स्थानांतरित करना।

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **लीड समय:** आदेश देने से लेकर बिक्री के लिए उपलब्ध सामान होने तक का बीता हुआ समय।

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **सुरक्षा स्टॉक:** मांग में वृद्धि और डिलीवरी में देरी के खिलाफ बफर के रूप में रखी गई अतिरिक्त इन्वेंटरी।

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **बुलव्हिप प्रभाव:** मांग में झूलों का प्रशस्ति जब आदेश स्टोर से आपूर्तिकर्ता की ओर जाते हैं।

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **विक्रेता-प्रबंधित इन्वेंटरी (VMI):** एक व्यवस्था जिसमें आपूर्तिकर्ता, खुदरा विक्रेता के बिक्री डेटा का उपयोग करके, तय करता है कि क्या और कब शिप करना है।

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **Q1 — X।** क्रॉस-डॉकिंग को भंडारण की अनुपस्थिति द्वारा परिभाषित किया गया है; उत्पाद आमतौर पर कुछ घंटों के भीतर निकल जाता है।

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b)।** बुलव्हिप प्रभाव मांग परिवर्तनशीलता का अपस्ट्रीम प्रशस्ति है, जो प्रत्येक लिंक द्वारा नीचे के लिंक के आदेश देने के कारण होता है बजाय वास्तविक अंतिम-ग्राहक मांग के।

segments.src: Sharing point-of-sale data is the standard remedy.*
segments.tr: बिक्री बिंदु डेटा साझा करना मानक उपचार है।*

es.title: [Retailing 101 #13] Nadie se percata de la cadena de suministro hasta que el estante está vacío

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > El producto real de un minorista no es solo lo que hay en el estante — es la capacidad de mantenerlo allí, día tras día, sin ahogarse en inventario.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Entra a cualquier supermercado y los estantes se ven sin esfuerzo.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: Esa es la ilusión.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Detrás de cada estante lleno hay una cadena de decisiones sobre *cuánto* mover, *cuándo* y *a dónde* — y un minorista que se equivoca en esas decisiones se queda sin producto o inmoviliza millones de dólares en cosas que nadie está comprando todavía.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Tres piezas componen la maquinaria.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: El centro de distribución (DC).** La mayoría de los minoristas de cadena no envían desde la fábrica a cada tienda.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Eso significaría que un proveedor de salsa picante envía pequeñas entregas a 400 direcciones separadas.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: En cambio, los proveedores envían camiones completos a un DC regional — un edificio grande, a menudo de 500,000 a 1 millón de pies cuadrados o más, generalmente ubicado cerca de autopistas para que un camión pueda llegar a sus tiendas en un día.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: El DC divide esos camiones y los reconstruye en cargas mixtas: un camión a una tienda, llevando papas fritas *y* toallas de papel *y* champú.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Menos camiones, camiones más llenos, menor costo por caja.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Una variante más rápida es **cross-docking**: el producto llega al muelle de entrada, se clasifica y sale en un camión de salida dentro de horas, sin entrar nunca en almacenamiento.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Excelente para productos de rápido movimiento y productos frescos; requiere coordinación muy estrecha, porque no hay amortiguador para ocultar errores.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Reabastecimiento.** Esta es la pregunta de cuándo hacer un nuevo pedido.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: La lógica clásica:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Si una tienda vende 20 unidades al día y tarda 3 días en obtener más, debe hacer un nuevo pedido de 60 unidades — más un colchón para cuando la demanda se dispara durante la semana o el camión llega tarde.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Ese colchón es **stock de seguridad**, y es un intercambio explícito: más stock de seguridad significa menos desabastecimientos y más efectivo sentado en un estante.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Hoy en día, la mayoría de esto funciona automáticamente con datos de escaneo en el punto de venta, por lo que el escáner de pago es un instrumento de cadena de suministro, no solo una caja registradora.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: Gestión de la cadena de suministro (SCM).** SCM es la capa de coordinación entre proveedores, DCs, transporte y tiendas — tratándolos como un sistema único en lugar de departamentos que se optimizan a sí mismos.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: El fracaso clásico que existe para prevenir es el **efecto látigo**: pequeñas oscilaciones en la demanda de los clientes se amplifican a medida que viajan aguas arriba.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Una tienda ve un aumento del 5%, ordena 10% más para estar segura, el DC ordena 20% más, el proveedor construye 40% más capacidad — y luego el aumento resulta ser nada.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Todos aguas arriba se quedan con inventario.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: La solución es la información: compartir datos de ventas reales en lugar de permitir que cada eslabón adivine a partir de los pedidos que recibe.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: Por eso existen arreglos como **inventario gestionado por el proveedor (VMI)**, donde el proveedor ve las ventas reales del minorista y decide qué enviar.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: Walmart y Procter & Gamble construyeron una versión temprana y bien conocida de esto a finales de los 80s, y el modelo se extendió por toda la industria.

segments.tr: Dos resultados, ambos costosos:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **Demasiado poco.** Encuentras un estante vacío, conduces a un competidor, y la cadena pierde una bolsa de $6 *más* la canasta de $80 que habrías llenado alrededor de ella. Investigaciones minoristas ampliamente citadas han situado las tasas promedio de desabastecimiento en el rango del 8% a nivel mundial — suena pequeño, pero impacta directamente en las ventas.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **Demasiado.** El lunes, la tienda tiene 200 bolsas extra de un bocadillo con vida útil medida en semanas, y se venderán con un 50% de descuento — vendidas por debajo del costo, más el efectivo que estuvo inmovilizado en ellas durante un mes.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: Ninguno aparece en el anuncio o en el diseño de la tienda.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: Ambos aparecen en el P&L.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **Centro de distribución (DC):** Una instalación que recibe envíos a granel de proveedores y los redistribuye como cargas mixtas listas para tienda.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking:** Mover bienes del muelle de entrada al muelle de salida con poco o ningún almacenamiento intermedio.

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **Tiempo de entrega:** El tiempo transcurrido desde la colocación de un pedido hasta tener los bienes disponibles para venta.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **Stock de seguridad:** Inventario adicional mantenido como amortiguador contra picos de demanda y retrasos en la entrega.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **Efecto látigo:** La amplificación de oscilaciones de demanda a medida que los pedidos viajan de tiendas a proveedores.

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **Inventario gestionado por el proveedor (VMI):** Un arreglo en el cual el proveedor, usando los datos de ventas del minorista, decide qué y cuándo enviar.

ar.title: [البيع بالتجزئة 101 #13] لا أحد يلاحظ سلسلة التوريد حتى يصبح الرف فارغًا

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > المنتج الحقيقي لبائع التجزئة ليس فقط ما يوجد على الرف — بل هو القدرة على الاحتفاظ به هناك، يومًا بعد يوم، دون الغرق في المخزون.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: ادخل أي متجر بقالة وستبدو الأرفف سهلة جدًا.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: هذا وهم.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: خلف كل رف ممتلئ توجد سلسلة قرارات حول *كم* كمية يتم نقلها، *متى*، و*إلى أين* — وبائع التجزئة الذي يخطئ في تلك القرارات إما يفقد المنتج أو يربط ملايين الدولارات في أشياء لم يشتريها أحد بعد.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: ثلاث قطع تشكل الآلية.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: مركز التوزيع (DC).** معظم بائعي التجزئة بالسلسلة لا ينقلون من المصنع إلى كل متجر.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: هذا يعني أن المورد الذي ينتج صلصة حارة يرسل شحنات صغيرة إلى 400 عنوان منفصل.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: بدلاً من ذلك، يرسل الموردون شاحنات كاملة إلى مركز توزيع إقليمي — مبنى كبير، غالبًا ما يتراوح بين 500,000 إلى مليون قدم مربع أو أكثر، يقع عادة بالقرب من الطرق السريعة حتى تتمكن الشاحنة من الوصول إلى متاجرها في يوم واحد.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: يقوم مركز التوزيع بتقسيم تلك الشاحنات وإعادة تجميعها إلى شحنات مختلطة: شاحنة واحدة إلى متجر واحد، تحمل رقائق *و* مناديل ورقية *و* شامبو.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: شاحنات أقل، شاحنات أكمل، تكلفة أقل لكل حالة.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: متغير أسرع هو **الشحن المباشر**: يصل المنتج إلى رصيف الاستقبال، يتم فرزه، ويغادر على شاحنة المغادرة في غضون ساعات، دون الدخول إلى التخزين.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: رائع للمنتجات سريعة الحركة والمنتجات الطازجة؛ لكنه يتطلب تنسيقًا محكمًا جدًا، لأنه لا يوجد عازل لإخفاء الأخطاء.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: إعادة التجديد.** هذا هو سؤال متى تعيد الطلب.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: المنطق الكلاسيكي:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: إذا كان متجر ما يبيع 20 وحدة في اليوم ويستغرق 3 أيام للحصول على المزيد، فيجب أن يعيد الطلب عند 60 وحدة — بالإضافة إلى وسادة لحالات ارتفاع الطلب في الأسبوع أو تأخر الشاحنة.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: هذه الوسادة هي **مخزون الأمان**، وهي مقايضة صريحة: مخزون أمان أكثر يعني نقصًا أقل في الأسهم وأموال أكثر معطلة على الرف.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: اليوم، يعمل معظم هذا تلقائيًا باستخدام بيانات مسح نقطة البيع، وهذا هو السبب في أن ماسح الدفع هو أداة في سلسلة التوريد، وليس مجرد آلة صراف.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: إدارة سلسلة التوريد (SCM).** إدارة سلسلة التوريد هي طبقة التنسيق عبر الموردين ومراكز التوزيع والنقل والمتاجر — معاملتها كنظام واحد بدلاً من أقسام تحسن نفسها كل على حدة.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: الفشل الكلاسيكي الذي توجد لمنعه هو **تأثير السوط**: التذبذبات الصغيرة في طلب العملاء تتضخم مع انتقالها بالعكس.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: متجر يرى ارتفاعًا بنسبة 5٪، فيطلب 10٪ أكثر للأمان، مركز التوزيع يطلب 20٪ أكثر، المورد يبني 40٪ طاقة أكثر — ثم يتضح أن الارتفاع لا شيء.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: الجميع بالعكس يتركون ممسكين بالمخزون.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: الحل هو المعلومات: شارك بيانات المبيعات الحقيقية بدلاً من السماح لكل رابط بالتخمين من الطلبات التي يتلقاها.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: هذا هو السبب في وجود ترتيبات مثل **المخزون الذي يديره المورد (VMI)**، حيث يرى المورد المبيعات الفعلية لبائع التجزئة ويقرر ما سيتم شحنه.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: بنت Walmart و Procter & Gamble نسخة مبكرة وشهيرة من هذا في أواخر الثمانينات، وانتشر النموذج عبر الصناعة.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: إنه يوم السبت قبل Super Bowl.

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: أنت في متجر بقالة خارج Phoenix، وتريد رقائق التورتيلا والصلصة.

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: إليك ما كان يجب أن ينجح.

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: قبل ثلاثة أسابيع، نظر مخطط الفئة إلى أرقام العام الماضي وتوقع أن هذا المتجر سيبيع ما يقرب من ستة أضعاف حجم رقائقه الطبيعي في نافذة يومين.

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: أثار هذا التنبؤ طلبيات شراء أكبر للمورد.

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: شحنت الرقائق بالشاحنات الكاملة إلى مركز التوزيع الخاص بالسلسلة بالقرب من الطريق السريع، حوالي 30 ميلاً.

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: طوال الليل، اختار عمال مركز التوزيع الصناديق لكل متاجر المنطقة وحملوا مقطورة مختلطة.

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: وصلت إلى متجرك في الساعة 4 صباحًا، وشحن الفريق عرض الزاوية قبل استيقاظك.

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: الآن اقلبها.

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: لنفترض أن التنبؤ كان خاطئًا بنسبة 40٪.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: نتيجتان، كلاهما مكلف:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **قليل جدًا.** تجد رفًا فارغًا، تذهب بسيارتك إلى منافس، وتخسر السلسلة كيسًا بقيمة 6 دولارات *بالإضافة إلى* السلة التي تساوي 80 دولارًا والتي كنت ستملأها حوله. وضعت أبحاث التجزئة المستشهد بها على نطاق واسع متوسط معدلات نفاد الأسهم في مكان ما حول 8٪ عالميًا — يبدو صغيرًا، لكنه يؤثر مباشرة على المبيعات.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **كثير جدًا.** بحلول يوم الاثنين، يوجد لدى المتجر 200 كيس إضافي من وجبة خفيفة مع عمر افتراضي يُقاس بالأسابيع، وسيتم بيعها بخصم 50٪ — مبيعة بأقل من التكلفة، بالإضافة إلى الأموال التي كانت معطلة فيها لمدة شهر.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: لا أي من هاتين النتيجتين يظهر في الإعلان أو تصميم المتجر.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: لكن كلاهما يظهر في بيان الدخل.

fr.title: [Retailing 101 #13] On ne remarque la chaîne d'approvisionnement que lorsque le rayon est vide

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > Le vrai produit d'un détaillant, ce n'est pas seulement ce qui est sur le rayon — c'est la capacité à le maintenir là, jour après jour, sans se noyer dans les stocks.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Entrez dans n'importe quel supermarché et les rayons semblent sans effort.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: C'est l'illusion.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Derrière chaque rayon plein se cache une chaîne de décisions sur *combien* déplacer, *quand*, et *vers où* — et un détaillant qui se trompe dans ces décisions soit manque de produit, soit bloque des millions de dollars dans des choses que personne n'achète encore.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Trois éléments composent le mécanisme.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: Le centre de distribution (CD).** La plupart des détaillants en chaîne ne livrent pas directement de l'usine à chaque magasin.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Cela signifierait qu'un fournisseur de sauce piquante envoie de petites livraisons à 400 adresses différentes.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: Au lieu de cela, les fournisseurs envoient des camions complets à un CD régional — un grand bâtiment, souvent de 500 000 à plus d'un million de pieds carrés, généralement situé près des autoroutes afin qu'un camion puisse atteindre ses magasins en un jour.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: Le CD décompose ces camions complets et les reconstitue en charges mixtes : un camion pour un magasin, transportant des chips *et* du papier toilette *et* du shampooing.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Moins de camions, des camions plus pleins, un coût par caisse moins élevé.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Une variante plus rapide est l'**empotage croisé** : le produit arrive au quai d'entrée, est trié, et repart sur un camion de sortie en quelques heures, sans jamais entrer en stockage.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Excellent pour les produits rapides et les produits frais ; cela nécessite une coordination très stricte, car il n'y a pas de marge pour cacher les erreurs.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Le réapprovisionnement.** C'est la question de savoir quand recommander.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: La logique classique :

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Si un magasin vend 20 unités par jour et qu'il faut 3 jours pour en obtenir plus, il devrait réapprovisionner à 60 unités — plus une marge pour la semaine où la demande augmente ou le camion est en retard.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Cette marge est le **stock de sécurité**, et c'est un compromis explicite : plus de stock de sécurité signifie moins de ruptures de stock et plus de liquidités immobilisées sur un rayon.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Aujourd'hui, la plupart de cela fonctionne automatiquement à partir des données de scan du point de vente, ce qui explique pourquoi le scanner de caisse est un instrument de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, pas seulement une caisse enregistreuse.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: La gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement (GCA).** La GCA est la couche de coordination entre les fournisseurs, les CD, le transport et les magasins — les traiter comme un seul système au lieu de départements qui s'optimisent chacun.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: L'échec classique qu'elle existe pour prévenir est l'**effet de fouet** : les petites fluctuations de la demande des clients s'amplifient en remontant.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Un magasin voit une augmentation de 5 %, commande 10 % de plus par prudence, le CD commande 20 % de plus, le fournisseur construit 40 % de capacité en plus — et puis l'augmentation s'avère être rien.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Tout le monde en amont se retrouve avec des stocks.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: La solution est l'information : partager les données de ventes réelles au lieu de laisser chaque maillon deviner d'après les commandes qu'il reçoit.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi existent des arrangements comme l'**inventaire géré par le fournisseur (IGF)**, où le fournisseur voit les ventes réelles du détaillant et décide ce qu'il faut expédier.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: Walmart et Procter & Gamble ont construit une version précoce et bien connue de ceci à la fin des années 1980, et le modèle s'est propagé dans l'industrie.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: C'est le samedi avant le Super Bowl.

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: Vous êtes dans un supermarché à l'extérieur de Phoenix, et vous voulez des tortillas chips et de la salsa.

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: Voici ce qui a dû fonctionner.

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: Il y a trois semaines, un planificateur de catégorie a examiné les chiffres de l'année dernière et prévu que ce magasin vendrait environ six fois son volume normal de chips en une fenêtre de deux jours.

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: Cette prévision a déclenché des commandes d'achat plus importantes au fournisseur.

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: Les chips ont été expédiées par camion au CD de la chaîne près de l'autoroute, à environ 30 miles.

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: Pendant la nuit, les travailleurs du CD ont prélevé des caisses pour chacun des magasins de la région et chargé une remorque mixte.

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: Elle est arrivée à votre magasin à 4 h du matin, et une équipe a rempli un présentoir d'extrémité avant que vous ne vous réveillez.

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: Maintenant, inversez.

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: Supposons que la prévision s'était trompée de 40 %.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: Deux résultats, tous deux coûteux :

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **Trop peu.** Vous trouvez un rayon vide, conduisez chez un concurrent, et la chaîne perd un sac de 6 $ *plus* le panier de 80 $ que vous auriez rempli autour. La recherche de détail largement citée a placé les taux de rupture de stock moyens quelque part dans la plage de 8 % dans le monde — cela semble peu, mais cela affecte directement les ventes.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **Trop beaucoup.** Arrivé lundi, le magasin a 200 sacs supplémentaires d'une collation avec une durée de conservation mesurée en semaines, et ils se vendront à 50 % de réduction — vendus en dessous du coût, plus les liquidités qui y ont été bloquées pendant un mois.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: Ni l'un ni l'autre n'apparaît dans la publicité ou la conception du magasin.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: Les deux apparaissent dans le compte de résultat.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Résumé en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. Les centres de distribution existent pour consolider les expéditions des fournisseurs en charges complètes et mixtes pour les magasins — réduisant le coût par caisse ; l'empotage croisé le fait sans rien stocker.

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. Le réapprovisionnement est un problème mathématique de délai de livraison et de stock de sécurité : trop peu signifie des ventes perdues, trop signifie des liquidités bloquées et des rabais.

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. La GCA coordonne l'ensemble de la chaîne et combat l'effet de fouet en partageant les données de demande réelles au lieu de laisser chaque maillon deviner.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **Centre de distribution (CD) :** Une installation qui reçoit des expéditions en vrac des fournisseurs et les redistribue sous forme de charges mixtes prêtes pour le magasin.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Empotage croisé :** Déplacer les biens du quai d'entrée au quai de sortie avec peu ou pas de stockage entre les deux.

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **Délai de livraison :** Le temps écoulé entre le placement d'une commande et la disponibilité des biens à la vente.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **Stock de sécurité :** Un inventaire supplémentaire maintenu comme tampon contre les pics de demande et les retards de livraison.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **Effet de fouet :** L'amplification des fluctuations de la demande à mesure que les commandes voyagent des magasins vers les fournisseurs.

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **Inventaire géré par le fournisseur (IGF) :** Un arrangement dans lequel le fournisseur, en utilisant les données de ventes du détaillant, décide quoi et quand expédier.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *Réponses : **Q1 — X.** L'empotage croisé est défini par l'absence de stockage ; le produit part généralement en quelques heures.

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b).** L'effet de fouet est l'amplification en amont de la variabilité de la demande, causée par chaque maillon commandant auprès du maillon en dessous plutôt qu'en fonction de la demande réelle du client final.

segments.src: Sharing point-of-sale data is the standard remedy.*
segments.tr: Partager les données du point de vente est le remède standard.*

pt.title: [Varejo 101 #13] Ninguém Nota a Cadeia de Suprimentos Até a Prateleira Ficar Vazia

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > O verdadeiro produto de um varejista não é apenas o que está na prateleira — é a capacidade de mantê-lo lá, dia após dia, sem se afogar em estoque.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Entre em qualquer supermercado e as prateleiras parecem fáceis.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: Essa é a ilusão.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Atrás de cada prateleira cheia há uma cadeia de decisões sobre *quanto* mover, *quando* e *para onde* — e um varejista que erra essas decisões ou fica sem produto ou prende milhões de dólares em coisas que ninguém está comprando ainda.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Três peças compõem a maquinaria.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: O centro de distribuição (CD).** A maioria dos varejistas em cadeia não envia da fábrica para cada loja.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Isso significaria um fornecedor de molho apimentado enviando pequenas entregas para 400 endereços separados.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: Em vez disso, os fornecedores enviam carregamentos completos para um CD regional — um prédio grande, geralmente com 500.000 a mais de 1 milhão de pés quadrados, geralmente localizado perto de rodovias para que um caminhão possa alcançar suas lojas em um dia.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: O CD divide esses carregamentos e os reconstrói em cargas mistas: um caminhão para uma loja, carregando batatas fritas *e* toalhas de papel *e* xampu.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Menos caminhões, caminhões mais cheios, menor custo por caixa.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Uma variante mais rápida é **cross-docking**: o produto chega no dock de entrada, é classificado e sai em um caminhão de saída em poucas horas, nunca entrando no armazenamento.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Ótimo para produtos de rápido movimento e produtos frescos; requer coordenação muito ajustada, porque não há buffer para esconder erros.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Reabastecimento.** Esta é a questão de quando reabastecer.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: A lógica clássica:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Se uma loja vende 20 unidades por dia e leva 3 dias para receber mais, seu ponto de reabastecimento deve ser 60 unidades — mais um amortecedor para picos de demanda semanais ou atrasos do caminhão.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Esse amortecedor é **estoque de segurança**, e é uma troca explícita: mais estoque de segurança significa menos falta de estoque e mais dinheiro parado em uma prateleira.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Hoje, a maioria disso funciona automaticamente com dados de varredura de ponto de venda, e é por isso que o scanner de checkout é um instrumento de cadeia de suprimentos, não apenas um caixa registrador.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: Gerenciamento da cadeia de suprimentos (GCS).** GCS é a camada de coordenação entre fornecedores, CDs, transporte e lojas — tratando-os como um sistema único em vez de departamentos que se otimizam independentemente.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: A falha clássica que existe para evitar é o **efeito chicote**: pequenas oscilações na demanda do cliente são amplificadas conforme viajam para o fornecedor.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Uma loja vê um aumento de 5%, pede 10% mais para estar segura, o CD pede 20% mais, o fornecedor constrói 40% mais capacidade — e então o aumento acaba não sendo nada.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Todos a montante ficam segurando estoque.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: A solução é informação: compartilhe dados de vendas reais em vez de deixar cada elo adivinhar dos pedidos que recebe.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: É por isso que existem arranjos como **inventário gerenciado pelo fornecedor (IGF)**, onde o fornecedor vê as vendas reais do varejista e decide o que enviar.
