in.title: [Retailing 101 #13] Orang Tidak Memperhatikan Rantai Pasokan Hingga Rak Kosong

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > Produk nyata pengecer bukan sekadar apa yang ada di rak — ini adalah kemampuan untuk menjaganya tetap ada, hari demi hari, tanpa tenggelam dalam persediaan.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Masuk ke supermarket mana pun dan rak-rak terlihat tanpa usaha.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: Itu adalah ilusi.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Di balik setiap rak yang penuh adalah rantai keputusan tentang *berapa banyak* untuk memindahkan, *kapan*, dan *ke mana* — dan pengecer yang membuat keputusan itu salah baik kehabisan produk atau mengikat jutaan dolar dalam barang yang belum dibeli siapa pun.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Tiga bagian membentuk mesin ini.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: Pusat distribusi (DC).** Sebagian besar pengecer rantai tidak mengirim dari pabrik ke setiap toko.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Itu berarti pemasok saus pedas mengirim pengiriman kecil ke 400 alamat terpisah.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: Sebaliknya, pemasok mengirim truk penuh ke DC regional — bangunan besar, sering kali 500.000 hingga lebih dari 1 juta kaki persegi, biasanya berlokasi dekat dengan jalan raya sehingga truk dapat mencapai tokonya dalam sehari.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: DC memecah muatan truk tersebut dan membangunnya kembali menjadi beban campuran: satu truk ke satu toko, membawa keripik *dan* handuk kertas *dan* sampo.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Lebih sedikit truk, truk lebih penuh, biaya lebih rendah per kasus.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Varian yang lebih cepat adalah **cross-docking**: produk tiba di dermaga masuk, disortir, dan meninggalkan truk keluar dalam beberapa jam, tidak pernah masuk penyimpanan.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Bagus untuk fast mover dan produk segar; diperlukan koordinasi yang sangat ketat, karena tidak ada buffer untuk menyembunyikan kesalahan.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Pengisian kembali (Replenishment).** Ini adalah pertanyaan tentang kapan harus memesan kembali.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: Logika klasik:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Jika toko menjual 20 unit per hari dan membutuhkan 3 hari untuk mendapatkan lebih banyak, harus memesan kembali di 60 unit — ditambah bantalan untuk lonjakan permintaan minggu atau truk terlambat.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Bantalan itu adalah **safety stock**, dan ini adalah perdagangan eksplisit: lebih banyak safety stock berarti lebih sedikit kehabisan stok dan lebih banyak uang tunai yang duduk di rak.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Saat ini sebagian besar ini berjalan otomatis dari data pemindaian penjualan poin, itulah sebabnya pemindai checkout adalah instrumen rantai pasokan, bukan hanya mesin kasir.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: Manajemen rantai pasokan (SCM).** SCM adalah lapisan koordinasi di seluruh pemasok, DC, transportasi, dan toko — memperlakukan mereka sebagai satu sistem bukan departemen yang masing-masing mengoptimalkan diri mereka sendiri.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Kegagalan klasik yang ada untuk mencegah adalah **efek cambuk**: goyangan kecil dalam permintaan pelanggan diperkuat saat mereka bepergian ke hulu.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Toko melihat lonjakan 5%, memesan 10% lebih banyak untuk aman, DC memesan 20% lebih banyak, pemasok membangun 40% lebih banyak kapasitas — dan kemudian lonjakan itu terbukti tidak ada.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Semua orang di hulu ditinggalkan memegang persediaan.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: Perbaikannya adalah informasi: bagikan data penjualan nyata alih-alih membiarkan setiap tautan menebak dari pesanan yang diterima.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: Itulah sebabnya pengaturan seperti **persediaan yang dikelola vendor (VMI)** ada, di mana pemasok melihat penjualan aktual pengecer dan memutuskan apa yang harus dikirim.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: Walmart dan Procter & Gamble membangun versi awal yang terkenal dari ini pada akhir 1980-an, dan model ini menyebar ke seluruh industri.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: Hari Sabtu sebelum Super Bowl.

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: Anda berada di supermarket di luar Phoenix, dan Anda menginginkan keripik tortilla dan salsa.

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: Inilah yang harus bekerja.

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: Tiga minggu lalu, seorang perencana kategori melihat angka tahun lalu dan meramalkan bahwa toko ini akan menjual kira-kira enam kali volume keripik normalnya dalam jendela dua hari.

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: Ramalan itu memicu pesanan pembelian yang lebih besar kepada pemasok.

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: Keripik dikirim dengan truk penuh ke DC rantai dekat jalan raya, sekitar 30 mil jauhnya.

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: Semalaman, pekerja DC memilih kasus untuk setiap toko di wilayah itu dan memuat truk campuran.

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: Tiba di toko Anda pada pukul 4 pagi, dan kru membongkar pajangan endcap sebelum Anda bangun.

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: Sekarang balikkan.

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: Misalkan ramalan itu salah 40%.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: Dua hasil, keduanya mahal:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **Terlalu sedikit.** Anda menemukan rak kosong, berkendara ke pesaing, dan rantai kehilangan tas $6 *ditambah* keranjang $80 yang akan Anda isi di sekitarnya. Penelitian ritel yang banyak dikutip telah menempatkan rata-rata tingkat kehabisan stok di suatu tempat di kisaran 8% di seluruh dunia — terdengar kecil, tetapi mendarat langsung di penjualan.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **Terlalu banyak.** Datang Senin, toko memiliki 200 kantong ekstra camilan dengan umur simpan diukur dalam minggu, dan mereka akan bergerak dengan diskon 50% — dijual di bawah biaya, ditambah uang tunai yang dikunci di dalamnya selama sebulan.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang muncul dalam iklan atau desain toko.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: Keduanya muncul dalam P&L.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. Pusat distribusi ada untuk mengkonsolidasikan pengiriman pemasok menjadi muatan truk penuh dan campuran untuk toko — mengurangi biaya per kasus; cross-docking melakukannya tanpa menyimpan apa pun.

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. Pengisian kembali adalah masalah matematika tentang waktu tunggu dan safety stock: terlalu sedikit berarti penjualan yang hilang, terlalu banyak berarti uang tunai mati dan penurunan harga.

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. SCM mengoordinasikan seluruh rantai dan melawan efek cambuk dengan berbagi data permintaan nyata alih-alih membiarkan setiap tautan menebak.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: 代わりに、供給業者は地域のDCに満杯のトラック積載量を送ります。大きな建物で、しばしば500,000から100万平方フィート以上で、通常は州間高速道路の近くに位置しているため、トラックは1日で店舗に到達できます。

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: DCはそれらのトラック積載量を分割し、混合荷物に再構築します。1つのトラックが1つの店舗に、チップス*と*ペーパータオル*とシャンプーを運びます。

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: トラックが少なく、満杯のトラック、ケースあたりのコストが低い。

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: より速い変種は**クロスドッキング**です。製品は到着ドックに到着し、分類され、数時間以内に出発ドックから出発します。保管に入ることはありません。

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: 高速移動商品と新鮮な農産物に最適です。エラーを隠すためのバッファがないため、非常に厳密な調整が必要です。

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: 補充**。これは再注文する時期についての質問です。

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: 古典的なロジック：

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: 店舗が1日に20ユニットを販売し、さらに取得するのに3日かかる場合、60ユニットで再注文する必要があります。週の需要スパイクまたはトラックが遅れた場合のためのクッション。

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: そのクッションは**安全在庫**で、明示的な取引です。安全在庫が多いほど、品切れが少なくなり、棚に多くの現金が座ります。

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: 今日、これのほとんどは販売時点スキャンデータから自動的に実行されます。これが、チェックアウトスキャナーがサプライチェーン機器であり、単なるレジスターではない理由です。

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: サプライチェーン管理(SCM)**。SCMは供給業者、DC、輸送、店舗全体の調整層です。各部門が自分たちを最適化する部門として扱うのではなく、1つのシステムとして扱っています。

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: それが防ぐために存在する古典的な失敗は**ブルウィップ効果**です。顧客需要の小さな変動は、上流に移動するにつれて増幅されます。

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: 店舗が5%の上昇を見て、安全のために10%多く注文し、DCが20%多く注文し、供給業者が40%多くの容量を構築します。そして、その上昇は何もないことが判明します。

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: 上流のすべてのユーザーが在庫を保持したままにされています。

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: 修正は情報です。受け取った注文から推測させるのではなく、実際の販売データを共有します。

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: これが、供給業者が小売業者の実際の売上を見て、何を配送するかを決定するような**ベンダー管理在庫(VMI)**のようなアレンジメントが存在する理由です。

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: WalmartとProcter & Gambleは1980年代後半にこれの初期の著名なバージョンを構築し、モデルは業界全体に広がりました。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: スーパーボウルの前の土曜日です。

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: Phoenixの外のスーパーマーケットにいて、トルティーヤチップスとサルサが欲しいです。

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: ここでは何が機能する必要があったかです。

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: 3週間前、カテゴリープランナーは昨年の数字を見て、このストアが2日間のウィンドウで通常のチップボリュームの約6倍を販売することを予測しました。

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: その予測により、供給業者への大きな購入注文がトリガーされました。

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: チップスは州間高速道路の近くのチェーンのDCにトラック積載量で配送され、約30マイル外です。

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: 一晩中、DCワーカーは地域の各店舗の事例を選んで、混合トレーラーに積み込みました。

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: 午前4時に店舗に到着し、起床する前にクルーがエンドキャップディスプレイに在庫を積みました。

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: 今度はそれを反転させます。

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: 予測が40%外れていたと仮定します。

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: 2つの結果、両方とも高額です：

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **あまりにも少ない。** 空の棚を見つけ、競合他社にドライブして、チェーンは$6バッグ*と*その周りに満たしたであろう$80バスケットを失います。広く引用される小売研究により、世界中の平均品切れ率は8%の範囲のどこかに置かれています。小さな音ですが、販売に直接着地します。

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **あまりにも多い。** 月曜日に来て、店舗は週で測定された棚寿命のスナックの200個の余分なバッグを持っており、それらは50%オフで移動します。原価以下で販売され、さらに1ヶ月間ロックアップされた現金。

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: どちらも広告や店舗設計には表示されません。

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: 両方ともP&Lに表示されます。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Distribution centers exist to consolidate supplier shipments into full, mixed truckloads for stores — cutting cost per case; cross-docking does it without storing anything.
segments.tr: 1. 流通センターは、供給業者の配送をケースあたりのコストを削減する店舗への完全な混合トラック積載量に統合するために存在します。クロスドッキングは何も保存することなくそれを行います。

segments.src: 2. Replenishment is a math problem about lead time and safety stock: too little means lost sales, too much means dead cash and markdowns.
segments.tr: 2. 補充はリードタイムと安全在庫についての数学問題です。あまりにも少ないということは売上が失われたということで、あまりにも多いということは死活現金とマークダウンを意味します。

segments.src: 3. SCM coordinates the whole chain and fights the bullwhip effect by sharing real demand data instead of letting each link guess.
segments.tr: 3. SCMはチェーン全体を調整し、各リンクに推測させるのではなく、実際の需要データを共有することでブルウィップ効果と戦っています。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **流通センター(DC)：** 供給業者からの一括配送を受け取り、混合のストア対応負荷として再配布する施設。

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **クロスドッキング：** 商品をインバウンドドックからアウトバウンドドックに、その間にほとんどまたはまったく保管されずに移動させます。

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **リードタイム：** 注文を置いてから商品が販売可能になるまでの経過時間。

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **安全在庫：** 需要スパイクと配達遅延に対するバッファとして保持される余分な在庫。

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **ブルウィップ効果：** 注文が店舗から供給業者に向かって移動するにつれて、需要スイングの増幅。

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **ベンダー管理在庫(VMI)：** 小売業者の販売データを使用して、供給業者が何を配送するかと時期を決定するアレンジメント。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *回答：**Q1 — X.** クロスドッキングは保管の欠落によって定義されます。製品は通常数時間以内に出発します。

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b).** ブルウィップ効果は、実際の最終顧客需要ではなく、下のリンクからの各リンク注文によって引き起こされる、需要変動性の上流増幅です。

segments.src: Sharing point-of-sale data is the standard remedy.*
segments.tr: 販売時点データの共有は標準的な救済策です。*

de.title: [Einzelhandel 101 #13] Niemand bemerkt die Lieferkette, bis das Regal leer ist

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > Das eigentliche Produkt eines Einzelhändlers ist nicht nur das, was im Regal steht — es ist die Fähigkeit, es dort zu halten, Tag für Tag, ohne in Lagerbeständen zu ersticken.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Betreten Sie einen beliebigen Supermarkt und die Regale sehen mühelos aus.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: Das ist die Illusion.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Hinter jedem vollen Regal steckt eine Reihe von Entscheidungen darüber, *wie viel* zu bewegen, *wann* und *wohin* — und ein Einzelhändler, der diese Entscheidungen falsch trifft, läuft entweder aus Produkten aus oder bindet Millionen Dollar in Dingen, die noch niemand kauft.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Drei Teile bilden die Maschinerie.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: Das Distributionszentrum (DZ).** Die meisten Einzelhandelsketten versenden nicht direkt von der Fabrik zu jedem Geschäft.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Das würde bedeuten, dass ein Lieferant von Chilisauce kleine Lieferungen zu 400 verschiedenen Adressen sendet.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: Stattdessen senden Lieferanten volle Lastwagen zu einem regionalen Distributionszentrum — ein großes Gebäude, oft 500.000 bis über 1 Million Quadratfuß, normalerweise in der Nähe von Autobahnen, damit ein Lastwagen seine Geschäfte an einem Tag erreichen kann.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: Das Distributionszentrum zerlegt diese Lastwagen und baut sie in gemischte Ladungen um: ein Lastwagen zu einem Geschäft, mit Chips *und* Papiertüchern *und* Shampoo.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Weniger Lastwagen, vollere Lastwagen, niedrigere Kosten pro Kasten.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Eine schnellere Variante ist **Cross-Docking**: Produkte kommen am Eingangsladebereich an, werden sortiert und verlassen einen Ausgangslastwagen innerhalb von Stunden, ohne jemals ins Lager zu gehen.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Großartig für schnelle Umsätze und frische Produkte; es erfordert sehr enge Koordination, da es keinen Puffer gibt, um Fehler zu verbergen.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Nachbestellung.** Dies ist die Frage, wann man nachbestellen soll.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: Die klassische Logik:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Geschäft 20 Einheiten pro Tag verkauft und es 3 Tage dauert, bis mehr ankommen, sollte es bei 60 Einheiten nachbestellen — plus ein Puffer für die Woche, wenn die Nachfrage in die Höhe schnellt oder der Lastwagen zu spät kommt.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Dieser Puffer ist **Sicherheitsbestand**, und es ist ein expliziter Kompromiss: mehr Sicherheitsbestand bedeutet weniger Ausverkäufe und mehr Bargeld, das auf einem Regal sitzt.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Heute läuft das meiste davon automatisch von Verkaufsstelle-Scandaten ab, weshalb der Kassierer-Scanner ein Lieferketteninstrument ist, nicht nur eine Kasse.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: Lieferkettenmanagement (LKM).** LKM ist die Koordinationsschicht über Lieferanten, Distributionszentren, Transport und Geschäfte — sie als ein System behandeln, statt als Abteilungen, die sich jeweils selbst optimieren.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Der klassische Fehler, den es verhindern soll, ist der **Peitscheneffekt**: kleine Schwankungen in der Kundennachfrage werden verstärkt, wenn sie stromaufwärts wandern.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Ein Geschäft sieht einen 5%-Anstieg, bestellt 10% mehr zur Sicherheit, das Distributionszentrum bestellt 20% mehr, der Lieferant baut 40% mehr Kapazität — und dann stellt sich heraus, dass der Anstieg nichts ist.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Jeder stromaufwärts sitzt auf Beständen fest.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: Die Lösung ist Information: Echte Verkaufsdaten teilen, statt jede Verbindung von den Bestellungen raten zu lassen, die sie erhält.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: Deshalb gibt es Vereinbarungen wie **vom Lieferanten verwaltetes Inventar (VMI)**, bei denen der Lieferant die tatsächlichen Verkäufe des Einzelhändlers sieht und entscheidet, was er versenden soll.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **Distributionszentrum (DZ):** Eine Einrichtung, die Großmengen-Sendungen von Lieferanten erhält und sie als gemischte, geschäftsfertige Ladungen umverteilt.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-Docking:** Verschieben von Waren vom Eingangsladebereich zum Ausgangsladebereich mit wenig oder keiner Lagerung dazwischen.

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **Lieferzeit:** Die verstrichene Zeit vom Aufgeben einer Bestellung bis zur Verfügbarkeit der Waren zum Verkauf.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **Sicherheitsbestand:** Zusätzlicher Bestand, der als Puffer gegen Nachfragespitzen und Lieferverzögerungen gehalten wird.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **Peitscheneffekt:** Die Verstärkung von Nachfrageschwankungen, wenn Bestellungen von Geschäften zu Lieferanten wandern.

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **Vom Lieferanten verwaltetes Inventar (VMI):** Eine Vereinbarung, bei der der Lieferant unter Verwendung der Verkaufsdaten des Einzelhändlers entscheidet, was und wann versendet wird.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **Q1 — X.** Cross-Docking ist durch das Fehlen von Lagerung definiert; Produkte verlassen normalerweise innerhalb von Stunden.

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b).** Der Peitscheneffekt ist die stromaufwärts Verstärkung der Nachfragevariabilität, verursacht dadurch, dass jede Verbindung von der Verbindung darunter bestellt, statt von der echten Endbenutzernachfrage.

vi.title: [Bán lẻ 101 #13] Không ai nhận ra Chuỗi cung ứng cho đến khi Kệ trống rỗng

segments.src: > A retailer's real product isn't just what's on the shelf — it's the ability to keep it there, day after day, without drowning in inventory.
segments.tr: > Sản phẩm thực của một nhà bán lẻ không chỉ là những gì trên kệ — đó là khả năng giữ nó ở đó, ngày này qua ngày khác, mà không chìm trong hàng tồn kho.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Walk into any supermarket and the shelves look effortless.
segments.tr: Bước vào bất kỳ siêu thị nào và các kệ trông như dễ dàng.

segments.src: That's the illusion.
segments.tr: Đó là ảo giác.

segments.src: Behind every full shelf is a chain of decisions about *how much* to move, *when*, and *to where* — and a retailer that gets those decisions wrong either runs out of product or ties up millions of dollars in stuff nobody is buying yet.
segments.tr: Đằng sau mỗi kệ đầy là một chuỗi quyết định về *bao nhiêu* để di chuyển, *khi nào*, và *đi đâu* — và một nhà bán lẻ mắc lỗi trong những quyết định đó hoặc hết sản phẩm hoặc buộc hàng triệu đô la vào những thứ mà chưa ai mua.

segments.src: Three pieces make up the machinery.
segments.tr: Ba phần tạo nên cơ chế.

segments.src: The distribution center (DC).** Most chain retailers don't ship from the factory to each store.
segments.tr: Trung tâm phân phối (DC).** Hầu hết các nhà bán lẻ chuỗi không gửi hàng từ nhà máy đến từng cửa hàng.

segments.src: That would mean a supplier of hot sauce sending small deliveries to 400 separate addresses.
segments.tr: Điều đó có nghĩa là một nhà cung cấp nước sốt cay gửi hàng nhỏ đến 400 địa chỉ riêng biệt.

segments.src: Instead, suppliers send full truckloads to a regional DC — a big building, often 500,000 to 1 million-plus square feet, usually sited near interstates so a truck can reach its stores in a day.
segments.tr: Thay vào đó, các nhà cung cấp gửi toàn bộ xe tải đến một DC khu vực — một tòa nhà lớn, thường từ 500.000 đến hơn 1 triệu feet vuông, thường nằm gần các đường cao tốc liên tiểu bang để một chiếc xe tải có thể tiếp cận các cửa hàng của nó trong một ngày.

segments.src: The DC breaks those truckloads apart and rebuilds them into mixed loads: one truck to one store, carrying chips *and* paper towels *and* shampoo.
segments.tr: DC chia những xe tải đó thành những phần và xây dựng lại chúng thành những lô hàng hỗn hợp: một xe tải đến một cửa hàng, chở chips *và* khăn giấy *và* dầu gội.

segments.src: Fewer trucks, fuller trucks, lower cost per case.
segments.tr: Ít xe tải hơn, xe tải đầy hơn, chi phí thấp hơn cho mỗi lô hàng.

segments.src: A faster variant is **cross-docking**: product arrives on the inbound dock, gets sorted, and leaves on an outbound truck within hours, never entering storage.
segments.tr: Một biến thể nhanh hơn là **cross-docking**: sản phẩm đến khu vực sàn tàu đến, được sắp xếp, và rời khỏi một chiếc xe tải đi trên trong vài giờ, không bao giờ đưa vào kho lưu trữ.

segments.src: Great for fast movers and fresh produce; it requires very tight coordination, because there's no buffer to hide mistakes.
segments.tr: Tuyệt vời cho những người di chuyển nhanh và sản phẩm tươi; nó yêu cầu sự phối hợp rất chặt chẽ, vì không có bộ đệm để che giấu lỗi.

segments.src: Replenishment.** This is the question of when to reorder.
segments.tr: Bổ sung.** Đây là câu hỏi khi nào để đặt hàng lại.

segments.src: The classic logic:
segments.tr: Logik cổ điển:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily sales x lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: If a store sells 20 units a day and it takes 3 days to get more, it should reorder at 60 units — plus a cushion for the week demand spikes or the truck is late.
segments.tr: Nếu một cửa hàng bán 20 đơn vị một ngày và mất 3 ngày để có thêm, nó nên đặt hàng lại ở 60 đơn vị — cộng với bộ đệm cho những lần tăng spike nhu cầu tuần hoặc xe tải muộn.

segments.src: That cushion is **safety stock**, and it's an explicit trade: more safety stock means fewer stockouts and more cash sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: Bộ đệm đó là **hàng tồn an toàn**, và nó là một giao dịch rõ ràng: nhiều hàng tồn an toàn hơn có nghĩa là ít thiếu hàng hơn và nhiều tiền hơn ngồi trên kệ.

segments.src: Today most of this runs automatically off point-of-sale scan data, which is why the checkout scanner is a supply chain instrument, not just a cash register.
segments.tr: Ngày nay, hầu hết điều này được chạy tự động từ dữ liệu quét điểm bán hàng, đó là lý do tại sao máy quét thanh toán là một công cụ chuỗi cung ứng, không chỉ là máy tính tiền.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM).** SCM is the coordination layer across suppliers, DCs, transportation, and stores — treating them as one system instead of departments that each optimize themselves.
segments.tr: Quản lý chuỗi cung ứng (SCM).** SCM là lớp phối hợp trên các nhà cung cấp, DC, vận chuyển và cửa hàng — coi họ là một hệ thống thay vì các bộ phận mà mỗi bộ phận tối ưu hóa chính mình.

segments.src: The classic failure it exists to prevent is the **bullwhip effect**: small wobbles in customer demand get amplified as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Thất bại cổ điển nó tồn tại để ngăn chặn là **hiệu ứng bullwhip**: những dao động nhỏ trong nhu cầu khách hàng được khuếch đại khi chúng di chuyển trở lên.

segments.src: A store sees a 5% bump, orders 10% more to be safe, the DC orders 20% more, the supplier builds 40% more capacity — and then the bump turns out to be nothing.
segments.tr: Một cửa hàng thấy một quả bumps 5%, đặt hàng 10% nhiều hơn để an toàn, DC đặt hàng 20% nhiều hơn, nhà cung cấp xây dựng công suất 40% hơn — và sau đó bumps hóa ra không có gì.

segments.src: Everyone upstream is left holding inventory.
segments.tr: Mọi người phía trên đều bị bắt giữ hàng tồn kho.

segments.src: The fix is information: share real sales data instead of letting each link guess from the orders it receives.
segments.tr: Sửa chữa là thông tin: chia sẻ dữ liệu bán hàng thực tế thay vì để cho mỗi liên kết đoán từ các đơn hàng nó nhận được.

segments.src: That's why arrangements like **vendor-managed inventory (VMI)** exist, where the supplier sees the retailer's actual sales and decides what to ship.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao các sắp xếp như **hàng tồn do nhà cung cấp quản lý (VMI)** tồn tại, nơi nhà cung cấp thấy bán hàng thực tế của nhà bán lẻ và quyết định những gì để gửi.

segments.src: Walmart and Procter & Gamble built an early, well-known version of this in the late 1980s, and the model spread across the industry.
segments.tr: Walmart và Procter & Gamble xây dựng một phiên bản sớm, nổi tiếng của điều này vào cuối những năm 1980, và mô hình lan truyền trên toàn ngành.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong cuộc sống hàng ngày

segments.src: It's the Saturday before the Super Bowl.
segments.tr: Đó là thứ Bảy trước Super Bowl.

segments.src: You're at a supermarket outside Phoenix, and you want tortilla chips and salsa.
segments.tr: Bạn đang ở một siêu thị bên ngoài Phoenix, và bạn muốn chips tortilla và salsa.

segments.src: Here's what had to work.
segments.tr: Đây là những gì phải làm việc.

segments.src: Three weeks ago, a category planner looked at last year's numbers and forecast that this store would sell roughly six times its normal chip volume in a two-day window.
segments.tr: Ba tuần trước, một nhà lập kế hoạch loại nhìn vào các số năm ngoái và dự báo rằng cửa hàng này sẽ bán khoảng sáu lần khối lượng chip bình thường của nó trong cửa sổ hai ngày.

segments.src: That forecast triggered larger purchase orders to the supplier.
segments.tr: Dự báo đó kích hoạt các đơn đặt mua lớn hơn cho nhà cung cấp.

segments.src: The chips shipped by the truckload to the chain's DC near the interstate, about 30 miles out.
segments.tr: Các chip được gửi bằng xe tải đến DC của chuỗi gần con đường liên tiểu bang, khoảng 30 dặm ra ngoài.

segments.src: Overnight, DC workers picked cases for each of the region's stores and loaded a mixed trailer.
segments.tr: Qua đêm, các công nhân DC chọn các trường hợp cho mỗi cửa hàng của khu vực và nạp một rơmooc hỗn hợp.

segments.src: It arrived at your store at 4 a.m., and a crew stocked an endcap display before you woke up.
segments.tr: Nó đến cửa hàng của bạn lúc 4 giờ sáng, và một đội ngũ tích trữ một màn hình endcap trước khi bạn thức dậy.

segments.src: Now flip it.
segments.tr: Bây giờ lật nó.

segments.src: Suppose the forecast was off by 40%.
segments.tr: Giả sử dự báo bị tắt 40%.

segments.src: Two outcomes, both expensive:
segments.tr: Hai kết quả, cả hai đều tốn kém:

segments.src: - **Too little.** You find an empty shelf, drive to a competitor, and the chain loses a $6 bag *plus* the $80 basket you would have filled around it. Widely cited retail research has put average out-of-stock rates somewhere in the range of 8% worldwide — small-sounding, but it lands directly on sales.
segments.tr: - **Quá ít.** Bạn tìm thấy một kệ trống, lái xe đến một đối thủ cạnh tranh, và chuỗi mất một chiếc túi $6 *cộng* rổ $80 bạn sẽ lấp đầy xung quanh nó. Nghiên cứu bán lẻ được trích dẫn rộng rãi đã đặt tỷ lệ hết hàng trung bình ở đâu đó trong khoảng 8% trên thế giới — nghe có vẻ nhỏ, nhưng nó rơi trực tiếp trên doanh số bán hàng.

segments.src: - **Too much.** Come Monday, the store has 200 extra bags of a snack with a shelf life measured in weeks, and they'll move at 50% off — sold below cost, plus the cash that was locked up in them for a month.
segments.tr: - **Quá nhiều.** Đến thứ Hai, cửa hàng có 200 túi thêm của một bữa ăn nhẹ với tuổi thọ trên kệ được đo bằng tuần, và họ sẽ di chuyển ở mức 50% giảm — bán dưới giá vốn, cộng với tiền mặt bị khóa trong chúng trong một tháng.

segments.src: Neither shows up in the ad or the store design.
segments.tr: Không ai xuất hiện trong quảng cáo hoặc thiết kế cửa hàng.

segments.src: Both show up in the P&L.
segments.tr: Cả hai đều xuất hiện trong P&L.

segments.src: - **Distribution center (DC):** A facility that receives bulk shipments from suppliers and redistributes them as mixed, store-ready loads.
segments.tr: - **Trung tâm phân phối (DC):** Một cơ sở nhận các lô hàng hàng loạt từ các nhà cung cấp và phân phối lại chúng dưới dạng các lô hàng hỗn hợp, sẵn sàng cho cửa hàng.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking:** Moving goods from the inbound dock to the outbound dock with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking:** Di chuyển hàng hóa từ bến tàu đến đến bến tàu đi với ít hoặc không có kho lưu trữ ở giữa.

segments.src: - **Lead time:** The elapsed time from placing an order to having the goods available to sell.
segments.tr: - **Thời gian dẫn trước:** Thời gian trôi qua từ khi đặt hàng đến khi có hàng hóa sẵn sàng để bán.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held as a buffer against demand spikes and delivery delays.
segments.tr: - **Hàng tồn an toàn:** Hàng tồn kho bổ sung được giữ như một bộ đệm chống lại những tăng đột ngột nhu cầu và trì hoãn giao hàng.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect:** The amplification of demand swings as orders travel from stores toward suppliers.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng bullwhip:** Sự khuếch đại của những dao động nhu cầu khi các đơn hàng di chuyển từ các cửa hàng hướng đến các nhà cung cấp.

segments.src: - **Vendor-managed inventory (VMI):** An arrangement in which the supplier, using the retailer's sales data, decides what and when to ship.
segments.tr: - **Hàng tồn kho do nhà cung cấp quản lý (VMI):** Một sắp xếp trong đó nhà cung cấp, sử dụng dữ liệu bán hàng của nhà bán lẻ, quyết định những gì và khi nào để gửi.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking is defined by the absence of storage; product typically leaves within hours.
segments.tr: *Câu trả lời: **Q1 — X.** Cross-docking được xác định bởi sự vắng mặt của kho lưu trữ; sản phẩm thường rời khỏi trong vài giờ.

segments.src: **Q3 — (b).** The bullwhip effect is the upstream amplification of demand variability, caused by each link ordering off the link below it rather than off real end-customer demand.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (b).** Hiệu ứng bullwhip là sự khuếch đại phía trên của tính thay đổi nhu cầu, được gây ra bởi mỗi liên kết đặt hàng từ liên kết dưới nó thay vì từ nhu cầu khách hàng cuối cùng thực tế.
